observations: Photo 0: A closed silver laptop with an Apple logo, held in hand. A pink sticker on the back reads 'MacBook Air 2022, M2, 16/512, P947X7D TFT, CC: 315 87%, Port: 1234'.

Photo 1: The same laptop open, showing a macOS login screen with a beach wallpaper. The keyboard is visible, with a Touch ID button on the right side of the spacebar. The screen has a noticeable reflection and glare.
Photo 2: A closer view of the back of the laptop, same pink sticker as in photo 0, with the same text. The Apple logo is slightly smudged or damaged.
The laptop appears to be a MacBook Air, based on design and sticker text.
The sticker includes a serial number-like code 'P947X7D TFT' and 'CC: 315 87%', which may refer to cycle count or battery health.
No visible damage to the body or screen from these angles, but reflections make screen condition hard to assess.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 2 show a pink sticker with 'MacBook Air 2022' written on it.
Photo 0 and photo 2 show 'M2' on the sticker.
Photo 0 and photo 2 show '16/512' on the sticker, which implies 16GB RAM.
Photo 0 and photo 2 show '16/512' on the sticker, which implies 512GB storage.
Photo 1 shows the login screen, but no proof of full functionality (e.g., booting into desktop, running apps, battery health).
Photo 2 sticker says 'CC: 315 87%', which is consistent with battery health reporting.

risks.risk: Battery health may be misrepresented or degraded beyond 87%.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the macOS Battery Health info (System Settings > Battery > Battery Health) showing the actual cycle count and condition.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if battery is degraded, possibly requiring replacement soon.

risks.risk: Screen damage or dead pixels not visible due to glare and reflections.
risks.proof: A photo of the screen with a solid white or black background, taken in good lighting, to check for dead pixels or cracks.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if screen has minor to moderate damage, reducing value.

risks.risk: The device may be stolen, gray market, or have a tampered serial number.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the serial number engraved on the bottom of the laptop, or a screenshot from Apple's Check Coverage page with the serial number.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if it is a gray market or unverified unit, with lower value and higher risk.

risks.risk: Keyboard or trackpad malfunction not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video showing the keyboard typing and trackpad scrolling and clicking.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if keyboard or trackpad may be faulty, reducing value.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the serial number engraved on the bottom of the laptop.
A screenshot from Apple's Check Coverage page with the serial number.
A photo of the screen with a solid white background to check for dead pixels or damage.
A video showing the keyboard typing and trackpad functioning.
A screenshot of the macOS Battery Health info showing cycle count and condition.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a MacBook Air with the claimed specs based on the sticker, but critical functionality and condition risks (battery, screen, serial authenticity, keyboard/trackpad) cannot be verified from the current photos. Proof is needed to price accurately and avoid hidden defects.
